 FALMOUTH (WGME) -- There's a new trail for people of all abilities at Maine Audubon.
 A ribbon cutting happened Monday morning at the Gilsland Farm Audubon Center in Falmouth.
 The 2,265-foot trail starts at the visitor center, traveling through forest, along a wooden boardwalk and into open meadows.
 Also read: Orchard Farm Ridge in Gorham up for sale 
 A spur trail also leads to a vista overlooking the Presumpscot River Estuary.
 The trail is five feet wide, has three bench rest stops and interpretive signs.
 Also read: Portland City Council considers putting new limits, regulations on data centers 
 “The goal is for it to be really inclusive and available to everyone, no matter what your level of birding, or mobility issues or vision or any of those things and of course, we will learn from this trail and make improvements on the next trail that we build,” Maine Audubon President Judy Camuso said.
 She says they plan to build a similar trail outside Bangor next summer.
